Definition: from G373; intermission; by implication, recreation:--rest.
BiblicalUsage: The word means rest, and it appears five times — twice as a promise and twice as its opposite. Jesus says take His yoke and learn of Him, and you shall find rest unto your souls; and Revelation says those who worship the beast have no rest day nor night. The same word is the rest the soul finds in Christ and the rest the lost never find.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for rest carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the contrast — rest for the soul in Christ, and no rest day nor night for those who refuse Him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
